title: Fixed-degree truncation for pro-étale sections
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a finite unital ring, and $W$ an object of the small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site]. Use a common larger universe in which this site is small. Write $A_X$ for the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)$ for the category of sheaves of left $A_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; no commutativity of $A$ is required. Put $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)=D(\mathcal C)$, the unbounded cochain derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. An $A_X$-module sheaf is called classical when its underlying sheaf of sets is classical in [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]: for every small cofiltered affine étale presentation $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ over $X$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_i H(U_i)\to H(U)$ is bijective (equivalently, an isomorphism of left $A$-modules).

Let $\Gamma_W:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be evaluation $H\mapsto H(W)$ followed by forgetting the scalar action. Write $R\Gamma(W,-)$ for its total right derived functor, computed by evaluating a K-injective resolution [def-sp-kinjective-bridge], and $H^q(W,H)=H^qR\Gamma(W,H[0])$. These cohomology groups carry their natural left $A$-module structures. They may be computed as underlying abelian groups; all displayed maps are $A$-linear, and an isomorphism of their underlying groups is equivalently an isomorphism of $A$-modules. Canonical truncations $\tau_{\ge N}$ and $\tau_{<N}=\tau_{\le N-1}$ use the convention of [def-kun-truncations]. Let $e\ge0$ be an integer such that $H^q(W,H)=0$ for every $q>e$ and every classical $A_X$-module sheaf $H$.

1. For every integer $b$, if $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ has classical cohomology sheaves and $H^q(L)=0$ for $q>b$, then $H^mR\Gamma(W,L)=0$ for every $m>b+e+1$.
2. If $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ has classical cohomology sheaves and $m,N$ are integers with $N<m-e-1$, then the canonical map
$$H^mR\Gamma(W,K)\longrightarrow H^mR\Gamma(W,\tau_{\ge N}K)$$
is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Transport classicality of module sheaves along the underlying-set sheaf isomorphism, using isClassical_iso_iff. This is the fully proved private helper classicalModule_of_iso.

source.place: Parts (1) and (2); same Postnikov/Roos argument, with the zero-endpoint Milnor case read directly from the Roos long exact sequence

proof.text: Prove finite_range_upper_bound for a triangulated functor and an isomorphism-invariant property P of the relevant cohomology objects. Induct on the natural bound for b-a. If b<a the object is zero by t-structure orthogonality. If a=b, identify it with H^b placed in degree b; the single-functor shift isomorphism and the functor shift isomorphism reduce H^r of its image to H^(r-b) of the degree-zero single object. Otherwise split with the canonical triangle tau_<b K -> K -> tau_>=b K. Its first object is in [a,b-1], its third in [b,b]. Homology isomorphisms transport P only on these retained intervals. The homology exact sequence with zero endpoints proves the inductive step. This helper is proved in Lean.

proof.text: Prove countable-product preservation of rightDerivedFunctor for an additive countable-product-preserving F from an abelian category with K-injective resolutions to one with exact countable products. Choose K-injective representatives using the existing derived-category K-injective representative theorem (the source-resolution assumption is already in the interface). Apply termwise_product_isKInjective_and_isLimit to their termwise product cone. The actual right-derived unit is invertible on each representative and the product. Naturality on the product projections identifies the image cone with the localized termwise F-image cone. F preserves the termwise product; derivedCategory_countableProducts_core makes its localization a limiting cone in the target. Transport this limit property along the unit and representing isomorphisms and use preservesLimitsOfShape_of_discrete. This is the fully proved private helper rightDerived_preserves_countable_products, generalized locally because the existing scheme-module statement does not apply to this ringed-site module category.

proof.text: Represent L by K and form the existing strict postnikovTower K, whose nth term is K.truncGE(-n). The homology formulas give its derived object lower bound -n and upper bound b. Inside [-n,b], the homology isomorphism induced by the quotient, together with homologyFunctorFactors and the representative isomorphism, transports classicality from L. Apply finite_range_upper_bound to derived evaluation, P = IsClassicalModuleSheaf, and hbound. Thus H^r of the derived evaluation of every tower term vanishes for r>b+e. No assertion of classicality for zero cohomology outside the retained interval is needed.

source.place: Parts (1) and (2); same Postnikov/Roos argument, with the zero-endpoint Milnor case read directly from the Roos long exact sequence

proof.text: Use products_derived to obtain a limiting localized termwise product cone of the strict Postnikov tower. Apply product preservation of derived evaluation from the proved helper, then product preservation of abelian-group derived homology from derivedCategory_countableProducts_core. The resulting limiting cone has all vertices zero in each degree r>b+e, so its point is zero. Apply derived evaluation to the distinguished mappingCocone triangle of the tower transition endomorphism. In the homology exact sequence, H^(m-1) of the product and H^m of the product are zero for m>b+e+1; exactness forces H^m of the evaluated Roos complex to be zero. This is exactly the zero-endpoint consequence of the Milnor sequence, obtained without constructing its auxiliary limit maps. Finally left_complete_quasiIso makes the canonical postnikovComparison invertible under Q; transport vanishing through that map and the representative isomorphism to L.

proof.text: For the second clause put L=tau_<N K. Only classicality in degrees at most N-1 is needed by the proved upper-bound helper, and the homology of truncLTι transports it from K in those degrees. The standard t-structure gives vanishing above N-1. Apply the upper-bound helper in degrees m and m+1. The inequality N<m-e-1 implies both required bounds. Derived evaluation sends the canonical triangleLTGE N K to a distinguished triangle; isIso_homologyMap_mor₂ gives the isomorphism of H^m of its second arrow, definitionally the canonical map displayed in the theorem.

split_report.summary: Expanded the finite-truncation induction and the product-preservation calculation for derived evaluation using existing K-injective and product statements; checked the abelian-group, rather than sheaf, Milnor sequence and the canonical truncation map. Made all coefficient, degree, universe and cohomology conventions explicit without changing either hypothesis or conclusion; retained arbitrary finite rings. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 2-3 realize the first paragraph of det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation.proof.md; Step 1 supplies the functor framework used there. Steps 4-5 expand its second paragraph (left completeness and derived sections preserving the Roos triangle). Step 6 realizes its displayed Milnor sequence and vanishing conclusion. Step 7 realizes part (2), including the canonical map. This is exactly step 2 of the unit sk-prop-pe-unbounded-classical.

Generic K-injective product theorem for an arbitrary abelian category, used in the product-preservation calculation.

lean.statement: theorem unbounded_classical_truncation (X : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type u) [Ring A] [Finite A] (W : X.ProEt) [HasDerivedCategory (coefficientModules X A)] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions (coefficientModules X A)] [HasDerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}] (e : ℕ) (hbound : ∀ (q : ℤ) (H : coefficientModules X A), IsClassicalModuleSheaf H → q > e → IsZero (sectionCohomology X A W q H)) : (∀ (L : DerivedCategory (coefficientModules X A)) (_hL : IsClassicalModuleComplex L) (b : ℤ), (∀ (q : ℤ), b < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (coefficientModules X A) q).obj L)) → ∀ (m : ℤ), b + e + 1 < m → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} m).obj ((derivedSections X A W).obj L))) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (coefficientModules X A)) (_hK : IsClassicalModuleComplex K) (m N : ℤ), N < m - e - 1 → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} m).map ((derivedSections X A W).map ((CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.truncGEπ DerivedCategory.TStructure.t N).app K))))
